title: Customer profile whose preferences map contains a notification_channels array
rationale: The flagship structural defect reduced to its minimum realistic form. One multi-element array inside an otherwise ordinary settings object converts the entire object into an array of fabricated rows with every scalar sibling duplicated. The flattened form is byte-identical to that of a genuine array of three objects, so the loss is in the wire format, not merely in the reconstructor.
catchesBugClass: The object-versus-array ambiguity of separator-only flattening; scalar duplication via repeat-last-value; row-count fabrication driven by an unrelated field length.
cannotCatch: It cannot show the severity scaling with two array-valued siblings of different lengths. It also cannot distinguish a format-level fix from a reconstructor-level hack that special-cases length-1 vectors.

predicted.detail: preferences becomes a three-element array with the scalars duplicated. Genuinely ambiguous on the wire, so a correct fix is a format change - but the same class of ambiguity in the KEY domain was treated as a bug worth a breaking change, and the value domain deserves the same verdict.
